findings.body:
**`findingDispositionView` can return `evidence: []`, which contradicts the adapter's contract.** (src/ops/review/findings.ts:255-260)

The doc comment on lines 229-230 says absent evidence is `null`, "never []". The schema accepts `evidence: []` on a v2 terminal finding. Line 171 checks only for `undefined`, and line 84 allows any string array. The view passes `[]` through unchanged. It also adds no `/evidence` availability entry. A reader then sees an empty proof for a terminal disposition and no signal that the evidence is missing.

Normalize an empty array to `null` in the view. Alternatively, reject an empty array in `validateFindingVersions` for terminal v2 findings. The view fix is the smaller change.

<details>
<summary>Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
-    retained === undefined || (typeof retained === 'string' && retained.trim() === '')
+    retained === undefined ||
+    (typeof retained === 'string' && retained.trim() === '') ||
+    (Array.isArray(retained) && retained.length === 0)
       ? null
```
</details>

findings.body:
**`findingDispositionView` omits the availability entry when `acceptedRisk` is `null`.** (src/ops/review/findings.ts:283)

Line 283 checks only `=== undefined`. The v2 validation at lines 164-170 requires terminal findings to carry `acceptedRisk`, and `null` means unknown (line 103). A valid v2 terminal finding with `acceptedRisk: null` therefore returns `acceptedRisk: null` with no `/acceptedRisk` availability entry. The adapter's contract is that a null value always has an availability reason. The message on line 286 also says null is unknown, so it should cover both values. The `reviewTrigger` branch on line 295 already handles both `undefined` and `null`.

<details>
<summary>Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
-  if (finding.acceptedRisk === undefined)
+  if (finding.acceptedRisk === undefined || finding.acceptedRisk === null)
```
</details>
